units.rightText: but one thing is needful: for Mary hath chosen the good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

units.rightText: And he said unto them, Take heed, and keep yourselves from all covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

units.leftText: He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
units.rightText: And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:

units.leftText: He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’
units.rightText: and he reasoned within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have not where to bestow my fruits?

units.leftText: He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
units.rightText: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my grain and my goods.

units.leftText: I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.”’
units.rightText: And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, be merry.

units.leftText: “But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’
units.rightText: But God said unto him, Thou foolish one, this night is thy soul required of thee; and the things which thou hast prepared, whose shall they be?

units.leftText: So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”
units.rightText: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.

units.leftText: He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor yet for your body, what you will wear.
units.rightText: And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on.

units.leftText: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.
units.rightText: For the life is more than the food, and the body than the raiment.

units.leftText: Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!
units.rightText: Consider the ravens, that they sow not, neither reap; which have no store-chamber nor barn; and God feedeth them: of how much more value are ye than the birds!

units.leftText: Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?
units.rightText: And which of you by being anxious can add a cubit unto the measure of his life?
leftNotes: 12:25 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.

units.leftText: If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
units.rightText: If then ye are not able to do even that which is least, why are ye anxious concerning the rest?

units.leftText: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
units.rightText: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they toil not, neither do they spin; yet I say unto you, Even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

units.leftText: But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?
units.rightText: But if God doth so clothe the grass in the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow is cast into the oven; how much more shall he clothe you, O ye of little faith?

units.leftText: “Don’t seek what you will eat or what you will drink; neither be anxious.
units.rightText: And seek not ye what ye shall eat, and what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.

units.leftText: For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.
units.rightText: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: but your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.

units.leftText: But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things will be added to you.
units.rightText: Yet seek ye his kingdom, and these things shall be added unto you.

units.leftText: “Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
units.rightText: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

units.leftText: Sell what you have and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
units.rightText: Sell that which ye have, and give alms; make for yourselves purses which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief draweth near, neither moth destroyeth.

units.leftText: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
units.rightText: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

units.leftText: “Let your waist be dressed and your lamps burning.
units.rightText: Let your loins be girded about, and your lamps burning;

units.leftText: Be like men watching for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.
units.rightText: and be ye yourselves like unto men looking for their lord, when he shall return from the marriage feast; that, when he cometh and knocketh, they may straightway open unto him.

units.leftText: Blessed are those servants whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you that he will dress himself, make them recline, and will come and serve them.
units.rightText: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them sit down to meat, and shall come and serve them.

units.leftText: They will be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch and finds them so.
units.rightText: And if he shall come in the second watch, and if in the third, and find them so, blessed are those servants.

units.leftText: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched and not allowed his house to be broken into.
units.rightText: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched, and not have left his house to be broken through.

units.leftText: Therefore be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you don’t expect him.”
units.rightText: Be ye also ready: for in an hour that ye think not the Son of man cometh.

units.leftText: Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”
units.rightText: And Peter said, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even unto all?

units.leftText: The Lord said, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the right times?
units.rightText: And the Lord said, Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall set over his household, to give them their portion of food in due season?

units.leftText: Blessed is that servant whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.
units.rightText: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.
units.rightText: Of a truth I say unto you, that he will set him over all that he hath.

units.leftText: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and to be drunken,
units.rightText: But if that servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;

units.leftText: then the lord of that servant will come in a day when he isn’t expecting him and in an hour that he doesn’t know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.
units.rightText: the lord of that servant shall come in a day when he expecteth not, and in an hour when he knoweth not, and shall cut him asunder, and appoint his portion with the unfaithful.

units.leftText: That servant who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,
units.rightText: And that servant, who knew his lord’s will, and made not ready, nor did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes;

units.leftText: but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.
units.rightText: but he that knew not, and did things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. And to whomsoever much is given, of him shall much be required: and to whom they commit much, of him will they ask the more.

units.leftText: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.
units.rightText: I came to cast fire upon the earth; and what do I desire, if it is already kindled?

units.leftText: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
units.rightText: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!

units.leftText: Do you think that I have come to give peace on the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.
units.rightText: Think ye that I am come to give peace in the earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:

units.leftText: For from now on, there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.
units.rightText: for there shall be from henceforth five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

units.leftText: They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
units.rightText: They shall be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother in law against her daughter in law, and daughter in law against her mother in law.

units.leftText: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.
units.rightText: And he said to the multitudes also, When ye see a cloud rising in the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it cometh to pass.

units.leftText: When a south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.
units.rightText: And when ye see a south wind blowing, ye say, There will be a scorching heat; and it cometh to pass.

units.leftText: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you don’t interpret this time?
units.rightText: Ye hypocrites, ye know how to interpret the face of the earth and the heaven; but how is it that ye know not how to interpret this time?

units.leftText: “Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
units.rightText: And why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?

units.leftText: For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
units.rightText: For as thou art going with thine adversary before the magistrate, on the way give diligence to be quit of him; lest haply he drag thee unto the judge, and the judge shall deliver thee to the officer, and the officer shall cast thee into prison.

units.leftText: I tell you, you will by no means get out of there until you have paid the very last penny. ”
units.rightText: I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou have paid the very last mite.
leftNotes: 12:59 literally, lepton. A lepton is a very small brass Jewish coin worth half a Roman quadrans each, which is worth a quarter of the copper assarion. Lepta are worth less than 1% of an agricultural worker’s daily wages.

units.leftText: Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
units.rightText: Now there were some present at that very season who told him of the Galilæans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?
units.rightText: And he answered and said unto them, Think ye that these Galilæans were sinners above all the Galilæans, because they have suffered these things?

units.leftText: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
units.rightText: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all in like manner perish.

units.leftText: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?
units.rightText: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them, think ye that they were offenders above all the men that dwell in Jerusalem?

units.leftText: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”
units.rightText: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

units.leftText: He spoke this parable. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.
units.rightText: And he spake this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came seeking fruit thereon, and found none.

units.leftText: He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down! Why does it waste the soil?’
units.rightText: And he said unto the vinedresser, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why doth it also cumber the ground?

units.leftText: He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
units.rightText: And he answering saith unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:

units.leftText: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”
units.rightText: and if it bear fruit thenceforth, well; but if not, thou shalt cut it down.

units.leftText: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.
units.rightText: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath day.

units.leftText: Behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years. She was bent over and could in no way straighten herself up.
units.rightText: And behold, a woman that had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years; and she was bowed together, and could in no wise lift herself up.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw her, he called her and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”
units.rightText: And when Jesus saw her, he called her, and said to her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

units.leftText: He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God.
units.rightText: And he laid his hands upon her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.

units.leftText: The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the multitude, “There are six days in which men ought to work. Therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”
units.rightText: And the ruler of the synagogue, being moved with indignation because Jesus had healed on the sabbath, answered and said to the multitude, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the day of the sabbath.

units.leftText: Therefore the Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! Doesn’t each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead him away to water?
units.rightText: But the Lord answered him, and said, Ye hypocrites, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?

units.leftText: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”
units.rightText: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound, lo, these eighteen years, to have been loosed from this bond on the day of the sabbath?

units.leftText: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed; and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
units.rightText: And as he said these things, all his adversaries were put to shame: and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

units.leftText: He said, “What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?
units.rightText: He said therefore, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I liken it?

units.leftText: It is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his own garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”
units.rightText: It is like unto a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his own garden; and it grew, and became a tree; and the birds of the heaven lodged in the branches thereof.

units.leftText: Again he said, “To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?
units.rightText: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?

units.leftText: It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened.”
units.rightText: It is like unto leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till it was all leavened.
leftNotes: 13:21 literally, three sata. 3 sata is about 39 liters or a bit more than a bushel.

units.leftText: He went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and traveling on to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And he went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and journeying on unto Jerusalem.

units.leftText: One said to him, “Lord, are they few who are saved?”
units.rightText: And one said unto him, Lord, are they few that are saved? And he said unto them,

units.leftText: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in and will not be able.
units.rightText: Strive to enter in by the narrow door: for many, I say unto you, shall seek to enter in, and shall not be able.

units.leftText: When once the master of the house has risen up and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’
units.rightText: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, open to us; and he shall answer and say to you, I know you not whence ye are;

units.leftText: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’
units.rightText: then shall ye begin to say, We did eat and drink in thy presence, and thou didst teach in our streets;

units.leftText: He will say, ‘I tell you, I don’t know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’
units.rightText: and he shall say, I tell you, I know not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.

units.leftText: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.
units.rightText: There shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and yourselves cast forth without.

units.leftText: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.
units.rightText: And they shall come from the east and west, and from the north and south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Behold, there are some who are last who will be first, and there are some who are first who will be last.”
units.rightText: And behold, there are last who shall be first, and there are first who shall be last.

units.leftText: On that same day, some Pharisees came, saying to him, “Get out of here and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”
units.rightText: In that very hour there came certain Pharisees, saying to him, Get thee out, and go hence: for Herod would fain kill thee.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Go and say to that fox, Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures to-day and to-morrow, and the third day I am perfected.

units.leftText: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’
units.rightText: Nevertheless I must go on my way to-day and to-morrow and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!
units.rightText: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killeth the prophets, and stoneth them that are sent unto her! how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her own brood under her wings, and ye would not!

units.leftText: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
units.rightText: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

units.leftText: When he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a sabbath to eat bread, that they were watching him.

units.leftText: Behold, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.
units.rightText: And behold, there was before him a certain man that had the dropsy.

units.leftText: Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
units.rightText: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath, or not?

units.leftText: But they were silent.
units.rightText: But they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go.

units.leftText: He answered them, “Which of you, if your son or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a well, and will not straightway draw him up on a sabbath day?

units.leftText: They couldn’t answer him regarding these things.
units.rightText: And they could not answer again unto these things.

units.leftText: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, and said to them,
units.rightText: And he spake a parable unto those that were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief seats; saying unto them,

units.leftText: “When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,
units.rightText: When thou art bidden of any man to a marriage feast, sit not down in the chief seat; lest haply a more honorable man than thou be bidden of him,

units.leftText: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.
units.rightText: and he that bade thee and him shall come and say to thee, Give this man place; and then thou shalt begin with shame to take the lowest place.

units.leftText: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.
units.rightText: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest place; that when he that hath bidden thee cometh, he may say to thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have glory in the presence of all that sit at meat with thee.

units.leftText: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
units.rightText: For every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

units.leftText: He also said to the one who had invited him, “When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back.
units.rightText: And he said to him also that had bidden him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, nor thy kinsmen, nor rich neighbors; lest haply they also bid thee again, and a recompense be made thee.

units.leftText: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;
units.rightText: But when thou makest a feast, bid the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:

units.leftText: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”
units.rightText: and thou shalt be blessed; because they have not wherewith to recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed in the resurrection of the just.

units.leftText: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”
units.rightText: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: But he said to him, “A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.
units.rightText: But he said unto him, A certain man made a great supper; and he bade many:

units.leftText: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’
units.rightText: and he sent forth his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.

units.leftText: They all as one began to make excuses.
units.rightText: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a field, and I must needs go out and see it; I pray thee have me excused.

units.leftText: “Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’
units.rightText: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them; I pray thee have me excused.

units.leftText: “Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’
units.rightText: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

units.leftText: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’
units.rightText: And the servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor and maimed and blind and lame.

units.leftText: “The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’
units.rightText: And the servant said, Lord, what thou didst command is done, and yet there is room.

units.leftText: “The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
units.rightText: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and constrain them to come in, that my house may be filled.

units.leftText: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper. For many are called, but few are chosen. ’”
units.rightText: For I say unto you, that none of those men that were bidden shall taste of my supper.
leftNotes: 14:24 RP MT includes the last sentence. TR, NU, and FH MT omit: For many are called, but few are chosen.

units.leftText: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,
units.rightText: Now there went with him great multitudes: and he turned, and said unto them,

units.leftText: “If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.
units.rightText: If any man cometh unto me, and hateth not his own father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.

units.leftText: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross and come after me, can’t be my disciple.
units.rightText: Whosoever doth not bear his own cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

units.leftText: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?
units.rightText: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doth not first sit down and count the cost, whether he have wherewith to complete it?

units.leftText: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation and isn’t able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,
units.rightText: Lest haply, when he hath laid a foundation, and is not able to finish, all that behold begin to mock him,

units.leftText: saying, ‘This man began to build and wasn’t able to finish.’
units.rightText: saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

units.leftText: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
units.rightText: Or what king, as he goeth to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and take counsel whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?

units.leftText: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy and asks for conditions of peace.
units.rightText: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and asketh conditions of peace.

units.leftText: So therefore, whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.
units.rightText: So therefore whosoever he be of you that renounceth not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.

units.leftText: “Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?
units.rightText: Salt therefore is good: but if even the salt have lost its savor, wherewith shall it be seasoned?

units.leftText: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
units.rightText: It is fit neither for the land nor for the dunghill: men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

units.leftText: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.
units.rightText: Now all the publicans and sinners were drawing near unto him to hear him.

units.leftText: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”
units.rightText: And both the Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.

units.leftText: He told them this parable:
units.rightText: And he spake unto them this parable, saying,

units.leftText: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?
units.rightText: What man of you, having a hundred sheep, and having lost one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?

units.leftText: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
units.rightText: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

units.leftText: When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’
units.rightText: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and his neighbors, saying unto them, Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost.

units.leftText: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
units.rightText: I say unto you, that even so there shall be joy in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine righteous persons, who need no repentance.

units.leftText: “Or what woman, if she had ten drachma coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?
units.rightText: Or what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a lamp, and sweep the house, and seek diligently until she find it?
leftNotes: 15:8 A drachma coin was worth about a days wages for an agricultural laborer.

units.leftText: When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost!’
units.rightText: And when she hath found it, she calleth together her friends and neighbors, saying, Rejoice with me, for I have found the piece which I had lost.

units.leftText: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”
units.rightText: Even so, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

units.leftText: He said, “A certain man had two sons.
units.rightText: And he said, A certain man had two sons:

units.leftText: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ So he divided his livelihood between them.
units.rightText: and the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of thy substance that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.

units.leftText: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.
units.rightText: And not many days after, the younger son gathered all together and took his journey into a far country; and there he wasted his substance with riotous living.

units.leftText: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.
units.rightText: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that country; and he began to be in want.

units.leftText: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
units.rightText: And he went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.

units.leftText: He wanted to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.
units.rightText: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.

units.leftText: But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
units.rightText: But when he came to himself he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish here with hunger!

units.leftText: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.
units.rightText: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight:

units.leftText: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’
units.rightText: I am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

units.leftText: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
units.rightText: And he arose, and came to his father. But while he was yet afar off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

units.leftText: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
units.rightText: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight: I am no more worthy to be called thy son.

units.leftText: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
units.rightText: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth quickly the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:

units.leftText: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;
units.rightText: and bring the fatted calf, and kill it, and let us eat, and make merry:

units.leftText: for this, my son, was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.
units.rightText: for this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

units.leftText: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
units.rightText: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.

units.leftText: He called one of the servants to him and asked what was going on.
units.rightText: And he called to him one of the servants, and inquired what these things might be.

units.leftText: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.

units.leftText: But he was angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and begged him.
units.rightText: But he was angry, and would not go in: and his father came out, and entreated him.

units.leftText: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.
units.rightText: But he answered and said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, and I never transgressed a commandment of thine; and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

units.leftText: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’
units.rightText: but when this thy son came, who hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou killedst for him the fatted calf.

units.leftText: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that is mine is thine.

units.leftText: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”
units.rightText: But it was meet to make merry and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

units.leftText: He also said to his disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager. An accusation was made to him that this man was wasting his possessions.
units.rightText: And he said also unto the disciples, There was a certain rich man, who had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he was wasting his goods.

units.leftText: He called him, and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give an accounting of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’
units.rightText: And he called him, and said unto him, What is this that I hear of thee? render the account of thy stewardship; for thou canst be no longer steward.

units.leftText: “The manager said within himself, ‘What will I do, seeing that my lord is taking away the management position from me? I don’t have strength to dig. I am ashamed to beg.
units.rightText: And the steward said within himself, What shall I do, seeing that my lord taketh away the stewardship from me? I have not strength to dig; to beg I am ashamed.

units.leftText: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from management, they may receive me into their houses.’
units.rightText: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.

units.leftText: Calling each one of his lord’s debtors to him, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my lord?’
units.rightText: And calling to him each one of his lord’s debtors, he said to the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?

units.leftText: He said, ‘A hundred batos of oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’
units.rightText: And he said, A hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bond, and sit down quickly and write fifty.
leftNotes: 16:6 100 batos is about 395 liters or 104 U. S. gallons.

units.leftText: Then he said to another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’
units.rightText: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, A hundred measures of wheat. He saith unto him, Take thy bond, and write fourscore.

units.leftText: “His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.
units.rightText: And his lord commended the unrighteous steward because he had done wisely: for the sons of this world are for their own generation wiser than the sons of the light.

units.leftText: I tell you, make for yourselves friends by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal tents.
units.rightText: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends by means of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when it shall fail, they may receive you into the eternal tabernacles.

units.leftText: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
units.rightText: He that is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much: and he that is unrighteous in a very little is unrighteous also in much.

units.leftText: If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
units.rightText: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

units.leftText: If you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?
units.rightText: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?

units.leftText: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will hold to one and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.”
units.rightText: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
leftNotes: 16:13 “Mammon” refers to riches or a false god of wealth.

units.leftText: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they scoffed at him.
units.rightText: And the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things; and they scoffed at him.

units.leftText: He said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Ye are they that justify yourselves in the sight of men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.

units.leftText: “The law and the prophets were until John. From that time the Good News of God’s Kingdom is preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
units.rightText: The law and the prophets were until John: from that time the gospel of the kingdom of God is preached, and every man entereth violently into it.

units.leftText: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one tiny stroke of a pen in the law to fall.
units.rightText: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away, than for one tittle of the law to fall.

units.leftText: “Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery. He who marries one who is divorced from a husband commits adultery.
units.rightText: Every one that putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and he that marrieth one that is put away from a husband committeth adultery.

units.leftText: “Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.
units.rightText: Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, faring sumptuously every day:

units.leftText: A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was taken to his gate, full of sores,
units.rightText: and a certain beggar named Lazarus was laid at his gate, full of sores,

units.leftText: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs came and licked his sores.
units.rightText: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table; yea, even the dogs came and licked his sores.

units.leftText: The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and that he was carried away by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: and the rich man also died, and was buried.

units.leftText: In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.
units.rightText: And in Hades he lifted up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.

units.leftText: He cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue! For I am in anguish in this flame.’
units.rightText: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am in anguish in this flame.

units.leftText: “But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that you, in your lifetime, received your good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But here he is now comforted and you are in anguish.
units.rightText: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and Lazarus in like manner evil things: but now here he is comforted, and thou art in anguish.

units.leftText: Besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, and that no one may cross over from there to us.’
units.rightText: And besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that they that would pass from hence to you may not be able, and that none may cross over from thence to us.

units.leftText: “He said, ‘I ask you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house—
units.rightText: And he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house;

units.leftText: for I have five brothers—that he may testify to them, so they won’t also come into this place of torment.’
units.rightText: for I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.

units.leftText: “But Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’
units.rightText: But Abraham saith, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

units.leftText: “He said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
units.rightText: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one go to them from the dead, they will repent.

units.leftText: “He said to him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, if one rise from the dead.

units.leftText: He said to the disciples, “It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!
units.rightText: And he said unto his disciples, It is impossible but that occasions of stumbling should come; but woe unto him, through whom they come!

units.leftText: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
units.rightText: It were well for him if a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.

units.leftText: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.
units.rightText: Take heed to yourselves: if thy brother sin, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.

units.leftText: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
units.rightText: And if he sin against thee seven times in the day, and seven times turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.

units.leftText: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
units.rightText: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.

units.leftText: The Lord said, “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
units.rightText: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye would say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou rooted up, and be thou planted in the sea; and it would obey you.

units.leftText: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table’?
units.rightText: But who is there of you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say unto him, when he is come in from the field, Come straightway and sit down to meat;

units.leftText: Wouldn’t he rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?
units.rightText: and will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?

units.leftText: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.
units.rightText: Doth he thank the servant because he did the things that were commanded?

units.leftText: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”
units.rightText: Even so ye also, when ye shall have done all the things that are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants; we have done that which it was our duty to do.

units.leftText: As he was on his way to Jerusalem, he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as they were on the way to Jerusalem, that he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.

units.leftText: As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.
units.rightText: And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, who stood afar off:

units.leftText: They lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
units.rightText: and they lifted up their voices, saying, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.

units.leftText: When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.
units.rightText: And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go and show yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, as they went, they were cleansed.

units.leftText: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
units.rightText: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, with a loud voice glorifying God;

units.leftText: He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
units.rightText: and he fell upon his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
units.rightText: And Jesus answering said, Were not the ten cleansed? but where are the nine?

units.leftText: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this foreigner?”
units.rightText: Were there none found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger?

units.leftText: Then he said to him, “Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Arise, and go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.

units.leftText: Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them, “God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;
units.rightText: And being asked by the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God cometh, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:

units.leftText: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
units.rightText: neither shall they say, Lo, here! or, There! for lo, the kingdom of God is within you.

units.leftText: He said to the disciples, “The days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
units.rightText: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it.

units.leftText: They will tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ Don’t go away or follow after them,
units.rightText: And they shall say to you, Lo, there! Lo, here! go not away, nor follow after them:

units.leftText: for as the lightning, when it flashes out of one part under the sky, shines to another part under the sky, so will the Son of Man be in his day.
units.rightText: for as the lightning, when it lighteneth out of the one part under the heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall the Son of man be in his day.

units.leftText: But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
units.rightText: But first must he suffer many things and be rejected of this generation.

units.leftText: As it was in the days of Noah, even so it will also be in the days of the Son of Man.
units.rightText: And as it came to pass in the days of Noah, even so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.

units.leftText: They ate, they drank, they married, and they were given in marriage until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
units.rightText: They ate, they drank, they married, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.

units.leftText: Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
units.rightText: Likewise even as it came to pass in the days of Lot; they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;

units.leftText: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky and destroyed them all.
units.rightText: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all:

units.leftText: It will be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
units.rightText: after the same manner shall it be in the day that the Son of man is revealed.

units.leftText: In that day, he who will be on the housetop and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away. Let him who is in the field likewise not turn back.
units.rightText: In that day, he that shall be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away: and let him that is in the field likewise not return back.

units.leftText: Remember Lot’s wife!
units.rightText: Remember Lot’s wife.

units.leftText: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.
units.rightText: Whosoever shall seek to gain his life shall lose it: but whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.

units.leftText: I tell you, in that night there will be two people in one bed. One will be taken and the other will be left.
units.rightText: I say unto you, In that night there shall be two men on one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.

units.leftText: There will be two grinding grain together. One will be taken and the other will be left.”
units.rightText: There shall be two women grinding together; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.

leftNotes: 17:36 Some Greek manuscripts add: “Two will be in the field: the one taken, and the other left.”
rightNotes: 17:36 Some ancient authorities add v. 36. There shall be two men in the field; the one shall be taken and the other shall be left. Mat 24:40

units.leftText: They, answering, asked him, “Where, Lord?”
units.rightText: And they answering say unto him, Where, Lord? And he said unto them, Where the body is, thither will the eagles also be gathered together.

units.leftText: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray and not give up,
units.rightText: And he spake a parable unto them to the end that they ought always to pray, and not to faint;

units.leftText: saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God and didn’t respect man.
units.rightText: saying, There was in a city a judge, who feared not God, and regarded not man:

units.leftText: A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’
units.rightText: and there was a widow in that city; and she came oft unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.

units.leftText: He wouldn’t for a while; but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect man,
units.rightText: And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man;

units.leftText: yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
units.rightText: yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest she wear me out by her continual coming.

units.leftText: The Lord said, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
units.rightText: And the Lord said, Hear what the unrighteous judge saith.

units.leftText: Won’t God avenge his chosen ones who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?
units.rightText: And shall not God avenge his elect, that cry to him day and night, and yet he is longsuffering over them?

units.leftText: I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
units.rightText: I say unto you, that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?

units.leftText: He also spoke this parable to certain people who were convinced of their own righteousness, and who despised all others:
units.rightText: And he spake also this parable unto certain who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and set all others at nought:

units.leftText: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
